title: What an acknowledgement promises
sub: One partition, three replicas. Columns are offsets in the log.

frames.caption: One partition, replicated on three brokers; broker 1 is the leader. Records 0 to 2 are on all three replicas. The high watermark (3) marks how far every in-sync replica has copied: consumers can read only below it (green).
A producer with acks=1 writes record d. The leader appends it and immediately acknowledges: the producer believes d is safe. The followers have not fetched it yet (orange: above the high watermark).
Broker 1 crashes before any follower copies d.
The controller makes broker 2, an in-sync replica, the new leader. Its log ends at c. New writes continue from offset 3: record e takes the slot d had.

When broker 1 recovers, it rejoins as a follower and truncates its log to match the new leader. Record d, which the producer was told had been written, is gone for good. That is the risk acks=1 accepts in exchange for lower latency.

One partition, replicated on three brokers; broker 1 is the leader. Records 0 to 2 are on all three replicas. The high watermark (3) marks how far every in-sync replica has copied: consumers can read only below it (green).
A producer with acks=all writes record d. The leader appends it, but does not acknowledge yet: it waits until every in-sync replica has fetched d.
Both followers fetch d. The high watermark advances to 4, and only now is the producer told the write succeeded.

Broker 1 crashes. Broker 2 takes over as leader, and it already has d. Nothing acknowledged is lost. With min.insync.replicas = 2, the leader refuses acks=all writes whenever fewer than 2 replicas are in sync, so an acknowledged record is always on at least 2 brokers.
